name: addTasksToProject
description: Create multiple tasks under missions (projects) in bulk. Use when Nour needs to break down a project into several specific tasks at once, or lock in a daily/weekly routine with multiple schedule blocks.

missionId.description: Fallback mission ID if not specified per-task

context.description: WHERE the task gets done, as a CODE - not a topic or description. Exactly one of: DESK · PHONE · SHOP · CAR · HOME · ANYWHERE.

effort.description: Time budget as a CODE, not a duration string. Exactly one of: M5 (5 min) · M15 (15 min) · M30 (30 min) · H1 (1 hour) · H2PLUS (2+ hours).

loopKind.description: ONCE = one-shot · DAILY = repeats every day · WEEKLY = repeats on set weekdays (also send recurringDays) · PROMISE = commitment to someone (also send promiseTo).

missionId.description: Specific mission ID for this task. Use to route different tasks to different missions (e.g. Health, Business, Personal)

name: analyzeCompetitiveIntel
description: Analyze competitive landscape for Nick's Tire. Identifies competitor vulnerabilities (Chanakya-style), GSC keyword opportunities, and threats. Returns market position, exploit strategies, and guidance.

name: analyzeComposure
description: Analyze the operator's emotional regulation and composure. Scores mood stability, drift control, decision quality under stress, recovery speed, and trigger management. Returns a 0-100 composure score with specific guidance.

name: analyzeFitness
description: Analyze Nour's workout CONSISTENCY from his OWN logged daily workout flags (daily check-in + /body, merged) over a window. Returns active-day count + rate (% of logged days), current streak, longest streak, average workouts/week, and a recent-vs-prior trend. This is workout-FREQUENCY ONLY — statenour logs a daily yes/no, NOT type, intensity, duration, or load — so it reads consistency, not training quality. Use when Nour asks about his workout consistency, whether he's training enough, or his streak. Honest about thin data.

name: analyzeGoals
description: Analyze Nour's active LifeGoals with the SMART framework (Specific/Measurable/Achievable/Relevant/Time-bound, each 1-5 -> S/A/B/C grade) plus progress and pace. Names each goal's weaknesses (e.g. targetValue=0 -> not measurable; no deadline -> not time-bound) with a concrete fix, and flags weak/unmeasurable goals across the portfolio. Use when Nour asks about his goals, whether they're well-formed/SMART, goal progress or quality, or 'are my goals any good / what's wrong with my goals'.

name: analyzeMentalHealth
description: Analyze Nour's mental/emotional wellbeing from his OWN logged data (mood, energy, sleep, stress, workouts, journal patterns) over a window. Returns a grounded mood trend, volatility, sleep/workout correlations, a NON-clinical 'concern level' with factors, and safe guidance. Use when Nour asks how he's doing emotionally, about mood/stress/burnout patterns, or 'am I okay'. NOT a diagnosis — it surfaces crisis resources and never predicts self-harm.

name: analyzePowerDynamics
description: Analyze Nour's power position across all relationships. Returns leverage scores (avg power balance, strongest/weakest positions, dependency ratio), influence metrics (plays executed, XP), network health (active/neglected/mentors/rivals), threats (drainers, rivals, unstable alliances), and concrete next moves. Use when Nour asks about power dynamics, leverage, relationship strategy, or 'who has power over me'.

name: analyzeSleep
description: Analyze Nour's sleep from his OWN logged nightly hours (daily check-in, with /body tracking as fallback) over a window. Returns average, consistency (SD), short-night count + %, accumulated sleep-debt vs a 7.5h target, the trend/direction, and best/worst night. Use when Nour asks how his sleep is, whether he's sleep-deprived, about his sleep trend or sleep debt. Honest about thin data (<5 nights).

name: analyzeTrends
description: Detect what's changing across ALL of Nour's tracked daily metrics (mood, energy, sleep, dailyScore, deep-work, drift, workouts + body: weight, body-fat, waist, stress) over a window. Returns per-metric direction (rising/flat/falling) + per-30-day change + a recent-vs-prior change-point, the TOP MOVERS (biggest normalized change), and notable pairwise correlations (|r|>=0.5, e.g. sleep<->mood). Honest about thin data (per-metric insufficient flag when <5 points). Use when Nour asks 'what's changing / trending / what's off lately / what moves together' across his metrics. Reports direction without moralizing (e.g. weight is context-dependent).

name: analyzeWeightTrend
description: Analyze Nour's weight + body-composition TREND from his OWN BodyTracking logs over a window. Returns weight trend + per-week rate, body-fat trend, waist trend, net change, and — if he has an active weight LifeGoal — the distance from his latest weight to the target. Reports direction WITHOUT judging it good/bad/healthy (whether up or down is 'progress' depends on his goal, not a moral prior). No BMR/TDEE/calorie math (statenour stores no height/age). Use when Nour asks about his weight, body-composition trend, or whether he's making progress on weight. Honest about thin data.

name: analyzeWorkHealth
description: Analyze Nour's work-pattern health from his OWN logs (deep-work blocks + drift incidents from the daily check-in; stress + energy from /body) over a window. Returns each metric's average + trend plus a NON-clinical 'strain signal' (low/elevated/high) that rises when high stress, high drift, and low energy co-occur. The strain signal is an explicit heuristic, NOT a burnout diagnosis or clinical assessment (it ships a disclaimer). Use when Nour asks about his work-pattern health, burnout risk, or whether he's overworking. Honest about thin data.

name: archiveGoal
description: Archive a LifeGoal (soft-delete · preserves CoachLog + GoalEvent history · recoverable). Use when Nour says 'drop this goal' / 'archive that goal'. Pre-Wave-28 the UI hard-deleted goals · now both UI + Nick use soft-delete.

titleQuery.description: Fuzzy match against active goal titles if goalId unknown.

name: arsenalDeepResearch
description: Multi-round autonomous research with citations.

name: arsenalMultiAgent
description: Spawn N parallel sub-agents + synthesize. Max 8. Staff sub-agents with persona keys: research-analyst, contrarian-critic, execution-planner, thought-partner, strategist, tactician, business-consultant, ghostwriter.

goal.description: The overall operator goal · seen by every sub-agent as context

subAgents.description: Array of sub-agent task assignments · max 8

name.description: Stable name for this sub-agent · e.g. 'pricing_analysis' or 'review_themes'

outputHint.description: Optional output-shape hint · e.g. 'bulleted list' or 'JSON with {a,b,c}'

persona.description: Optional persona key from the typed library · e.g. 'research-analyst', 'contrarian-critic', 'thought-partner', 'tactician', 'business-consultant', 'ghostwriter'

task.description: Specific task for this sub-agent · 1-2 sentences · ≤800 chars

name: arsenalNotebookLM
description: Use Google NotebookLM via the connected MCP server. Allows deep grounding against custom uploaded source documents. Use 'notebookAlias' to route to specialized Memory Vaults.

action.description: The NotebookLM MCP tool to call (e.g., 'ask_question', 'list_notebooks')

notebookAlias.description: Target a specific memory vault. If provided, the system will inject the correct notebook_id.

name: arsenalPreTaskFanout
description: Pre-task 3-lens fan-out (research+risk+plan).

brainContext.description: Optional brain context to ground the lenses

question.description: The hard question to fan out on

name: arsenalResearch
description: Use Grok (xAI) for real-time analysis and research. Powered by the Arsenal integration chain.

query.description: Research question or topic to analyze

name: arsenalWebSearch
description: Web search with AI summarization. Tries Tavily first; falls back to Perplexity/Google, then to the multi-source quorum if those are unavailable. Powered by the Arsenal integration chain.

name: browseAndDo
description: Run a COMPLETE browser task autonomously: opens a cloud browser, plans + executes the steps (navigate, click, type, read), and returns a structured receipt with a session replay URL. THE preferred tool whenever Nour asks Nick to do something on a website ('go check X', 'find Y on site Z', 'fill the form but don't submit'). permission: 'read' = look only · 'draft' (default) = interact but STOP before any consequential submission (submit/send/purchase/delete) · 'execute' = allowed to fire the final action. Costs real money per step — keep goals specific.

goal.description: Specific, self-contained description of what to accomplish, including the site if known.

keepSessionOpen.description: Leave the session open (live-view) instead of closing it at the end.

permission.description: Action permission. Use 'execute' ONLY when Nour explicitly authorized the final consequential action.

startUrl.description: URL to open first (skips one planning step).

name: browser_do
description: LOW-LEVEL: start a live cloud browser session (headless Chrome) and return its id + live-view URL — you then drive it manually with browser_navigate. For complete tasks ('go check X online', 'pull data from Z') PREFER browseAndDo, which runs the whole workflow in one call. Use this only for surgical multi-tool control or debugging.

goal.description: Plain-English description of what the browser agent should accomplish. Will be stored on the session for later reference.

keepAlive.description: If true (default), session stays open even when idle so Nour can watch. Close it manually via /api/browser/session DELETE.

name: browser_navigate
description: Navigate the active cloud browser session to a URL. Requires a sessionId from a prior browser_do call. Returns the final resolved URL + page title. Use this to reach a specific page.

sessionId.description: Session id from a prior browser_do call.

url.description: Full URL to navigate to (including https://).

waitUntil.description: When to consider navigation complete. Default: networkidle.

name: checkAntiPattern
description: Check the anti-pattern library for lessons that match the current intent. Call BEFORE any side-effecting tool (sendSMS, createPaymentLink, triggerFollowUp, createQuote, runDeviceCommand) if Nour's intent rhymes with a past failure. Returns zero-or-more matching lessons with severity and lesson text — surface them to Nour before acting. Zero cost per call (pure DB).

domain.description: Restrict to one domain if you know it; omit to search all.

intent.description: One-sentence description of the action about to be taken, or the decision context.

name: checkCommitments
description: Check all active commitments — what's on track, what's overdue, what needs follow-up. Use proactively to hold Nour accountable.

name: classifyThought
description: Classify a thought into one of: raw, thinking, reasoning, insight, decision, reflection, planning, venting. Use when Nour asks 'what am I doing right now' or 'am I overthinking this'. Does NOT store anything — pure classification. Example: {"text":"maybe I should redo the whole homepage again"}

name: clearMit
description: Clear today's MIT so Nour can pick a new one. Usually only called if Nour explicitly says the MIT is wrong.

name: compareLiveRevenue
description: Compare live revenue across two date ranges using nickstire data. Use for 'this week vs last week' or 'this month vs last month'

name: completeCommitment
description: Mark a commitment as completed. Use when Nour confirms he did something he promised.

name: completeTask
description: Mark a task as done. DAILY tasks bump streak + lastCompletedAt and stay READY (loop reappears tomorrow). ONCE/PROMISE flip to DONE. Example: {"taskId":142}

name: composeEmail
description: Draft an email for Nour to review and explicitly send. NEVER auto-sends — returns a draft card the user clicks Send on. If Gmail is configured, also creates a draft in Nour's Gmail drafts directly via the Gmail API. Use when Nour says 'email X about Y', 'draft a note to ...', or asks for a written follow-up. If subject/body are not provided, the tool uses the `intent` to ask Nick to draft them in his next reply turn (preferred path: Nick writes the draft inline and passes it here as subject + body).

body.description: Plain-text email body. Markdown is OK; will render as plain text.

tone.description: Tone hint shown on the draft card so Nour can sanity-check at a glance

name: createCommitment
description: Create a new commitment — a promise made to a specific person with an optional deadline. Example: {"toWhom":"Nick","description":"send the Q3 tire order by Friday","deadline":"2026-08-15"}

name: createMissionPlan
description: Create a mission with multiple linked tasks in one call. Use when Nour describes a multi-step project or goal. `tasks` must hold AT LEAST ONE task — an empty array is rejected and nothing is created, so if the steps are not known yet, create the tasks later with addTasksToProject rather than sending [].

domain.description: Which life area this mission belongs to. Exactly one of: BUSINESS · PERSONAL · HEALTH · CONTENT · FINANCE.

context.description: WHERE the task gets done, as a CODE - not a topic or description. Exactly one of: DESK · PHONE · SHOP · CAR · HOME · ANYWHERE.

effort.description: Time budget as a CODE, not a duration string. Exactly one of: M5 (5 min) · M15 (15 min) · M30 (30 min) · H1 (1 hour) · H2PLUS (2+ hours).

loopKind.description: ONCE = one-shot · DAILY = repeats every day · WEEKLY = repeats on set weekdays (also send recurringDays) · PROMISE = commitment to someone (also send promiseTo).

name: createTask
description: Create a new task. Use when Nour needs to do something specific. Set `loopKind` to DAILY for habits, PROMISE for commitments to someone (set `promiseTo`), ONCE for one-shot work. Link to a goal via `goalId` so completing it auto-lifts the goal. Example: {"title":"Call Meineke about the lift quote","loopKind":"ONCE","priority":30}

context.description: WHERE the task gets done, as a CODE - not a topic or description. Exactly one of: DESK · PHONE · SHOP · CAR · HOME · ANYWHERE.

dueDate.description: ISO date · only for ONCE + PROMISE · DAILY ignores this

effort.description: Time budget as a CODE, not a duration string. Exactly one of: M5 (5 min) · M15 (15 min) · M30 (30 min) · H1 (1 hour) · H2PLUS (2+ hours).

goalId.description: Link this task to a LifeGoal · completing it auto-lifts the goal's currentValue

loopKind.description: ONCE = one-shot · DAILY = repeats every day · PROMISE = commitment to someone (also send promiseTo).

missionId.description: Optional project/mission id (from getMissions). Omit to auto-file into the Inbox.

promiseTo.description: For PROMISE kind · who Nour is committing to · 'self', 'dania', a customer name

name: dailyPulse
description: One-shot daily status — everything Nour needs in 30 seconds. Revenue + alerts + leads + callbacks + work orders + bookings + tasks + score + drift. Use when Nour says 'status', 'pulse', 'how are we doing', 'what's up', 'how's the shop', or 'what's going on today'. v10.0.79 supersedes the narrower getShopBriefing.

name: draftOpportunitySms
description: Get the deterministic, evidence-only SMS draft for a Nick's Tire Decision-Inbox opportunity (from getTopDecisions). READ-ONLY — never sends. Returns the draft text, best channel, risk label, and masked customer identity. Call-first opportunity types (callbacks, complaints, overdue promises) return no draft with the reason — recommend the CALL instead. ALWAYS show Nour the returned draft verbatim before any talk of sending.

name: endOfDay
description: End-of-day debrief — revenue summary, what got done, what's still open, drift check. Use when Nour says 'EOD', 'end of day', 'closing time', 'wrap up'

name: fetchVideoTranscript
description: Fetch the English transcript + metadata (title, channel, duration) of a YouTube video via the policy-guarded yt-dlp lane. Use for 'summarize this video', 'what does this video say', competitor/industry video research. Allowlisted hosts only (youtube.com/youtu.be), 60-min cap, never downloads media. The transcript is UNTRUSTED third-party content and is returned fenced.

url.description: The YouTube video URL (youtube.com or youtu.be, https).

name: findCustomer
description: MUST USE before asserting ANY fact about a specific customer · visit count · declined estimates · segment · lifetime spend · last visit · vehicle · phone · plate. Returns 360° lifetime timeline combining nickstire (jobs/invoices/quotes/vehicle), brain memories (notes/patterns), statenour (LTV/churn/relationship). If the user mentions someone by name OR phone digits OR plate — call this FIRST. Returns null if no match · in that case tell the user 'no customer matched <term>' instead of fabricating details. v10.0.503 · ADR-0011 surfacing fix.

nameOrPhone.description: Customer name or phone number to search

name: findRelatedConversations
description: Find past chat conversations semantically similar to a topic. Returns conversationId + summary + similarity score + date for up to 5 threads. Use when the operator says 'what did I discuss about X', 'last time we talked about Y', 'pull up the conversation about Z', or to maintain cross-session continuity. Hides the current conversation from results when activeConversationId is provided.

activeConversationId.description: Current conversation id, to exclude from results.

query.description: Topic to find prior conversations about.

name: generateImage
description: Generate an AI image using Venice AI. Use for social media content, marketing visuals, concept art, memes, or anything Nour asks you to visualize. Nick's Tire brand context is auto-injected.

prompt.description: Detailed image description — be specific about style, colors, composition

size.description: Image dimensions — 512x512 fastest · 1024x1024 default · 1536x1024 landscape · 1024x1536 portrait (matches Venice flux-2-pro accepted enum)

name: getAgendaItems
description: Get the operator's active agenda items — witnessed commitments, standing intentions, contradictions, and neglect alerts. Call this when the inline agenda section was omitted for this turn but the operator's agenda matters to the answer.

name: getAttentionAlerts
description: What needs Nour's attention NOW — stale leads, unanswered callbacks, overdue WOs

name: getBlindSpots
description: Get severity-ranked blind spots — the things Nour is NOT paying attention to. Returns overdue commitments, stale leads, workout gaps, scoring gaps, neglected people, drift alerts. Use this when Nour asks 'what am I missing' or when you need to proactively surface a gap.

severity.description: Filter by severity. LOWERCASE only, exactly one of: critical, high, medium, low, all.

name: getBodyData
description: Get recent body tracking entries

name: getBrainHealth
description: Get a full brain health report — memory count, learning velocity, prediction accuracy, wisdom promotions, contradiction resolution. Shows how smart the brain is getting.

name: getCameraIntelligence
description: Get camera intelligence — shop traffic, vehicle counts, alerts, bay utilization, employee arrivals

name: getCommitments
description: Get active commitments

name: getContextualGreeneLaws
description: Get the top 3 Robert Greene laws applicable to a specific person right now, with rationale and concrete actions. Use when reasoning about relationship strategy for a specific contact.

name: getCronStatus
description: Get status and health of all cron jobs

name: getDarkPsychologyTactics
description: Look up dark psychology tactics (cognitive biases, manipulation techniques, social engineering patterns) relevant to the operator's current situation. Returns matching entries with triggers, actions, and applicability. Use when Nour asks about persuasion, influence, manipulation, cognitive biases, or tactical social dynamics.

query.description: Situation or topic to find matching tactics for

name: getDashboardSummary
description: Get full business dashboard summary — revenue, customers, reviews, open jobs

name: getDriftAlerts
description: Get unresolved drift alerts

name: getEmotionalState
description: Get Nour's current emotional arc — stress trajectory, dominant state, triggers, decision risk. Shows how emotions are affecting performance.

name: getEstimateLeaks
description: Find revenue leaks — estimates that never became invoices (customers who got a quote but didn't convert). This is money walking out the door.

daysBack.description: How many days back to check

name: getExternalWorkerJob
description: Read one previously queued NOUR external-worker job, including durable queue status, bounded result payload, error state, and Reality Ledger phase receipts.

name: getExternalWorkerLanes
description: Read the live NOUR external-worker plane: Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, and the local Qwen gateway. Reports measured runner freshness, auth/health/quota state, and cost class. No worker is executed.

name: getFinancialSnapshot

name: getFleetTruth

READ-ONLY. Use when the operator asks 'is everything running', 'system status', 'are the crons alive', or before claiming any scheduled capability works.

name: getGscSummary
description: Real Google Search Console totals for nickstire.org over a date range — clicks, impressions, CTR, average position. Use whenever Nour asks how SEO is performing, traffic, search visibility, or rankings overall. Defaults to last 30 days if no dates given. Numbers are derived from raw click+impression sums (not avg-of-avg) so multi-day totals are accurate. Position is impression-weighted.

name: getGscTopQueries
description: Top search queries driving organic traffic to nickstire.org from Google Search. Returns each query's clicks, impressions, CTR, and average position. Use whenever Nour asks 'what searches bring people in', 'top keywords', 'what people search for', or 'which queries convert'. Defaults to top 10 over the last 30 days.

name: getHabitRevenueCorrelation
description: Show how personal habits (workouts, discipline, energy) correlate with business outcomes (revenue, conversion, lead response). e.g. 'weeks with 4+ workouts = 23% higher revenue'.

name: getHabitStreaks
description: Get habit completion data — current streaks for daily-loop tasks (workouts, journal, etc).

name: getHealthToday
description: Today's health snapshot: sleep, weight, workout (BodyTracking) plus steps, resting heart rate and HRV from Apple Health samples, with last-sync freshness

name: getMarketingAttribution
description: Source-by-source attribution for Nick's Tire & Auto leads. Returns lead count + conversion count + conversion rate + revenue + avg ticket per source (popup / chat / booking / callback / sms / etc.) ranked by total dollars. Use whenever Nour asks 'what's working', 'which channel is converting', 'ROI per source', 'where are leads coming from', or 'what's our best marketing'. Defaults to last 30 days.

name: getMasteryScores
description: Get current mastery domain scores

name: getMissionDetail
description: Get ONE mission with its real progress: task counts by state, the next physical actions, deadline health, and its retro if it was archived. Use when Nour asks how a specific mission or project is going, or which one is stalled.

missionId.description: Mission id. Omit to match by title.

title.description: Partial title match when the id is unknown.

name: getMissions
description: Get active missions

name: getPowerBalanceSummary
description: Get power-balance scores for the top 5 people by interaction count. Returns each person's name, power balance (-1 to +1), and whether it's manually locked. Use when reasoning about relationship leverage across the network.

name: getRecentReflections
description: Get recent reflections generated by the cron reflection engine. These are meta-cognitive insights (what patterns changed this week, what's drifting, what predictions came true). Use when Nour asks 'what have I been learning' or 'what's my pattern lately'. Returns actionable + unacknowledged first.

limit.description: How many to return. MAXIMUM 20 - a larger value is rejected.

scope.description: LOWERCASE only, exactly one of: daily, weekly, monthly, triggered, all. Note: "personal" is NOT valid.

name: getRepoMap
description: Get the key file paths and architecture of a repo. Use when you need to understand where things are before making changes. Returns the project structure map.

name: getRevenueStats
description: Get revenue statistics for a given period

name: getReviewStats
description: Get Google Reviews statistics for Nick's Tire & Auto

name: getShopSnapshot
description: Get real-time shop data from the nickstire bridge — bookings, leads, revenue, callbacks, sync health

name: getSkillProtocol

Returns { ok, name, protocol } or { ok:false } when the skill has no bundled protocol.

name.description: Exact skill name from suggestSkills, e.g. 'maxforge-alpha'.

name: getSleepTrend
description: Sleep-hours series over the last N days (BodyTracking canonical, Apple Health-fed) with coverage count

name: getTasks
description: Get active tasks with their missions

name: getTodaySchedule
description: Get the operator's Google Calendar events for today and the next few days. Returns event titles, times, locations, attendees. Use when answering 'what's on my schedule', 'when is X meeting', or reasoning about availability.

daysAhead.description: How many days forward to fetch. Default 1 (today + tomorrow).

name: getTopDecisions
description: Read the shop's top revenue decisions from the nickstire opportunity queue — the same due-aware, consent-filtered, SQL-ranked top-5 the admin Decision Inbox shows. READ-ONLY. Use when the operator asks 'what should I decide', 'what's in the inbox', 'top opportunities', or before recommending any revenue action.

name: getWeeklyTargets
description: Get this week's 3 targets to check progress. Use mid-week to reference what was set on Monday.

name: githubListFiles
description: List files in a directory of a GitHub repo. Use to explore repo structure.

name: githubListRepos
description: List Nour's GitHub repos sorted by most recently updated.

name: githubReadFile
description: Read a file from any of Nour's GitHub repos. Use to inspect code, configs, or data files.

name: githubRecentCommits
description: Get recent commits from a repo. Use to see what changed recently.

name: githubSearchCode
description: Search for code across a GitHub repo. Use to find functions, variables, patterns.

query.description: Search query (code, function name, variable, etc.)

name: ingestDocumentFromUrl
description: Fetch a public document from a URL and ingest it into the operator's document index. Returns the documentId and a chunk count. Use when the operator says 'read this PDF' / 'index this doc' and shares a link. Supports PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, MD. Max 20MB.

filename.description: Optional override for the stored filename. Defaults to the URL path.

url.description: Direct download URL for the document.

name: invokeTool
description: Run a READ-ONLY tool by name that isn't loaded this turn (find it with searchTools first). Refuses anything that mutates state — write tools must load through the normal path so approval gates apply. Example: {"name":"getHabitStreaks","args":{}}

args.description: Arguments matching the tool's input schema.

name: journalDecision
description: Log a decision Nour just made during this conversation. Records the what, why, stakes, and chosen option so the Decision Pattern Analyzer can learn from it. Use this whenever Nick helps Nour make a choice.

name: last30days
description: Search and research a topic across live social platforms (Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, YouTube) and grounded web results from the last 30 days. Returns a raw data report with community comments and source coverage. Use this for queries about recent trends, public consensus, sentiment, product comparison, or tracking what individuals/companies are doing recently. The tool returns a raw structured report; you MUST synthesize it into a clean, markdown-formatted narrative with blue command-clickable links on first mention per the returned instructions. Do not dump the raw clusters.

deepResearch.description: Use Perplexity Deep Research (requires API key setup, spendy).

githubUser.description: Optional target GitHub username for person-mode.

subreddits.description: Comma-separated broad/category subreddit names to search.

topic.description: The research topic or search query.

xHandle.description: Optional target X handle for a person/product.

name: logSituation
description: Log a real situation for strategic analysis — AI matches relevant Greene laws and provides tactical advice

context.description: What KIND of situation this is (not a location — unrelated to the task `context` field). Exactly one of: business · personal · negotiation · conflict · decision.

situation.description: What happened or what decision you're facing

name: moneyprinter

Uses MoneyPrinterTurbo to write the video script, select royalty-free B-roll clips, synthesize voice narration (Azure edge_tts), and render subtitle overlays. Returns a success status with the generated video filepath. Use when Nour asks to create a video, generate a TikTok/Reel, write and synthesize B-roll, or output a short video on a topic.

language.description: Video script/voice language code (e.g. 'en', 'zh'). Defaults to auto-detect.

paragraphCount.description: Optional paragraph count for script segments. Default: 3.

script.description: Optional custom video script text. By default, script is auto-generated by AI.

subject.description: The main topic/keyword of the video. E.g., 'Why exercise is important'.

name: pinMemory
description: Pin a fact to long-term memory · creates a BrainMemory(category=pinned_user) row · surfaces in the brain's pinned context panel + chat recall. Use when Nour says 'remember this' / 'pin this' / 'this is important'.

content.description: The fact or note to pin · plain English · 1-2 sentences ideal

key.description: Optional dedup key · defaults to slug of content first 60 chars

name: proposeCalendarEvent
description: Create or propose a new Google Calendar event. If Google Calendar API is configured, writes the event directly to the calendar via the Google Calendar API. If not configured, returns a 'create event' URL with all fields pre-filled for the operator to click and create. Use when Nour wants to schedule something concrete (a focus block, a meeting, a follow-up).

endISO.description: Event end in ISO 8601. If omitted, defaults to startISO + 60 minutes.

startISO.description: Event start in ISO 8601 (e.g. '2026-05-13T14:00:00-04:00'). If timezone omitted, operator's local zone is assumed.

name: queryNickstire
description: Query live data from nickstire.org. Queries: revenue_today, revenue_range, leads_today, leads_pipeline, leads_urgent, bookings_today, bookings_status, customer_search, callbacks_pending, work_orders_active, attention_needed, shop_pulse, feature_flags, gsc_summary, gsc_top_queries. Money: customer_search.totalSpent is integer CENTS — quote totalSpentDollars. gsc_summary.source says whether totals are Google's official property total or a partial stored-row subset.

query.description: Query name from the list above

name: queueDeepResearch
description: Queue deep research to run in the background — returns immediately; the cited report arrives as a push notification in ~2 minutes. Use when the operator says 'go research X' / 'look into X and get back to me' and doesn't need the answer in this reply.

name: queueMissionExecution
description: Queue bounded durable background execution for an existing ACTIVE mission. V1 supports checkpoint and deep-research steps only; it survives chat closure/redeploys through Inngest, records progress to the Reality Ledger, and NEVER marks the mission complete automatically.

name: rankNextActions
description: Rank the top N open tasks by impact × ease × freshness. Use when Nour says 'what should I do next' or when there are more than 5 open tasks. Returns a sorted list with score + reasoning.

name: resolveAlert
description: Resolve a drift alert

name: resolveContradiction
description: Close an open claim-vs-record contradiction after Nour answers a CLAIM VS RECORD, ONE OPEN CONTRADICTION or CONTRADICTION ASKED EARLIER block. Required: contradictionKey 'tbl:<id>' from that block. side 'current_wins' = the record is right, 'old_wins' = the claim is outdated, 'dismissed' = ignore. 'both_valid' is not offered: it does not apply to these rows. A key without the tbl: prefix is not found.

contradictionKey.description: The key from the contradiction block ('tbl:<id>').

currentBelief.description: Not stored for table rows (the answer itself is the record). Leave empty.

note.description: Not stored for table rows (the table has no note column). Leave empty.

side.description: How Nour answered a claim-vs-record row. current_wins = the record is right (his claim was wrong). old_wins = the claim is outdated (it was true once, things moved on). dismissed = ignore it. both_valid does not apply to these rows.

name: reviewDecisionReplay
description: Review a past decision — record what happened, score the outcome, and extract the lesson.

lesson.description: What was learned from this decision

outcome.description: What actually happened since the decision

name: runCode
description: Execute JavaScript in a sandbox. Use for calculations, data analysis, projections, formatting. Has the JavaScript built-ins plus helpers avg, sum, min, max, pct, delta. No network, filesystem or modules (code containing the word import is refused). 5s limit. The code runs as a function body: use `return <value>` for the result, which comes back as JSON; console.log lines come back as logs.

code.description: JavaScript function body. Use `return <value>` for the result; without a return the result is null.

name: runDeviceCommand
description: Queue a smart-home command to a physical device (lights, locks, cameras, thermostats). Use when Nour says things like 'lock the front door', 'turn off the shop lights', 'take a snapshot'. Identify the device by name OR location + type — Nick resolves to the closest match.

command.description: Verb — turn_on | turn_off | toggle | lock | unlock | snapshot | record | arm | disarm | siren_on | siren_off | set_temp | set_brightness | speak.

deviceId.description: Preferred — the SmartDevice.id if Nick already has it.

deviceType.description: Narrow by type: LIGHT, LOCK, CAMERA, THERMOSTAT, SPEAKER, HEATER, APPLIANCE. Combines with locationQuery.

locationQuery.description: Fuzzy match against SmartDevice.location. 'shop' → matches 'shop', 'home-shop', etc.

nameQuery.description: Fuzzy match against SmartDevice.name (case-insensitive). 'front door' → matches 'Front Door Lock'.

params.description: Optional. E.g. { brightness: 70 } or { celsius: 22 } or { text: 'you forgot your keys' }.

name: runSimulation
description: Run a 'what if' simulation — predict the cascade of consequences for a specific scenario. e.g. 'What if I hire a second tech?' or 'What if I raise prices 10%?'

name: scheduleFollowUp
description: Schedule a customer follow-up task with a deadline. Use when Nour says 'follow up with X in N days' or 'remind me to call customer Y'. Creates a task in the Inbox mission with a due date.

daysFromNow.description: How many days from now the follow-up is due

effort.description: Time budget as a CODE, not a duration string. Exactly one of: M5 (5 min) · M15 (15 min) · M30 (30 min) · H1 (1 hour) · H2PLUS (2+ hours).

name: scoreLocation
description: Evaluate a candidate address for a second shop. Returns a 0-100 score, tier (A=ship · F=don't), strongest + weakest dimension, and operator-facing reasoning. Five dimensions: footTrafficPercentile (0-100) · reviewDensity (reviews per nearby competitor) · competitorCluster (count within 2mi · lower=better) · driveTimeToHomeMinutes (to Euclid HQ · lower=better) · zoningFriction (0-100 · lower=better). Missing dimensions are scored neutrally (0.5) with an explicit warning. Use this when the operator says 'score this location', 'evaluate Cleveland address', 'second location', 'expansion address', or asks whether a specific spot is viable. Pure compute · no external data fetched · operator supplies the measured params.

address.description: Candidate address · street + city is enough

competitorCluster.description: Count of auto-repair shops within 2 miles · LOWER is better

driveTimeToHomeMinutes.description: Drive time in minutes from Euclid HQ · LOWER is better · capped at 60

reviewDensity.description: Reviews per nearby competitor · higher is better · saturates ~20

zoningFriction.description: Estimated municipal hassle 0-100 · LOWER is better

name: scrapeWebPage
description: Scrape a web page and convert it to clean markdown. Use when the operator shares a URL and says 'read this', 'what does this page say', 'summarize this link', or when Nick needs to understand the content of a specific web page. Returns the page content as markdown with title and description. Requires FIRECRAWL_API_KEY — returns a clear error if not configured.

excludeTags.description: CSS selectors to exclude from output. e.g. ['nav', 'footer', '.ads'].

url.description: The URL to scrape and convert to markdown.

waitFor.description: Wait time in ms for JS-heavy pages to render. Default 0. Use 3000-5000 for SPAs.

name: searchColdMemory
description: Semantic search across Nour's cold memory corpus — archived Google Drive docs, old brain memories, and ingested knowledge. Unlike searchMemories (keyword), this is meaning-based: 'my pipeline is drying up' correctly finds getRevenueAging-style memories without needing the literal word. USE THIS when Nour asks about something you don't see in the hot system prompt, when he references an old document, or when the question requires reaching back into historical knowledge. Returns top matches with similarity scores and Drive view URLs when available.

minScore.description: Minimum hybrid score cutoff — below this is noise

query.description: Natural language query — describe what you're looking for

scope.description: Source bucket to search. 'drive' = Google Drive ingested docs only. 'ingest' = drive + gmail + calendar. 'all' = every brain memory. Default is 'drive' for focused archival lookup.

name: searchDocuments
description: Search across documents the operator has uploaded (PDFs, Word docs, spreadsheets, text files). Returns the top matching chunks with their source filename and a similarity score. Use when the operator references 'that PDF', 'the spreadsheet', or asks a question that likely answers from an uploaded document.

limit.description: How many top chunks to return. Default 5.

query.description: The natural-language question or topic to search for.

name: searchGreeneLaws
description: Search the 189 Greene strategic laws by keyword. Returns matching laws with essence and shop/personal application.

book.description: Filter by book: FORTY_EIGHT_LAWS, THIRTY_THREE_STRATEGIES, HUMAN_NATURE, MASTERY, ART_OF_SEDUCTION, FIFTIETH_LAW

query.description: Search term — title, concept, or situation

name: searchMemories
description: Search Nick's brain memories by keyword, category, or confidence threshold. Use to recall past insights, patterns, and stored knowledge. Example: {"query":"supplier pricing decision","limit":5}

asOf.description: ISO date. Answer AS OF that date: what was believed then, including beliefs corrected since, and nothing saved after it. Omit for current truth.

category.description: Filter by category: insight, pattern, preference, lesson, fact

limit.description: How many to return. MAXIMUM 50 - a larger value is rejected.

query.description: Keyword to search in memory content and keys

name: searchReflections
description: Search Nour's reflective writing — Reflection insights AND BrainDump entries (raw thoughts + summaries + detected patterns). Use when Nour asks 'have I thought about this before', 'what did I say about X last week', or wants past brainstorms / vents. Returns matches with source (reflection vs brain_dump) + date. Optional date range narrows the scope.

limit.description: How many to return. MAXIMUM 20 - a larger value is rejected.

name: searchTools
description: Find tools that are NOT currently loaded this turn. Use when you need a capability you don't see in your available tools — search by what you want to do (e.g. 'sleep data', 'github commits', 'customer lookup'). Returns matching tool names + schemas. Read-only tools can then be run via invokeTool; write tools require asking the operator to rephrase so the tool loads normally. Example: {"query":"habit streaks"}

query.description: What you want to do, plain words. Matched against tool names, categories and descriptions.

name: searchWebVerified
description: Cross-verified web search across multiple sources (Perplexity + Tavily + Exa + Google Grounding). Returns consensus when sources agree, or flags the disagreement when they diverge. Use for factual claims where being wrong matters: news, statistics, recent events, technical specs. Confidence ≥0.66 means 2+ sources agree. Prefer this over single-source web search when the operator's question is verifiable.

domains.description: Allowed domains for sources that support filtering.

query.description: The natural-language question or claim to verify.

recency.description: Time bound for results. Default any.

sources.description: Restrict to these sources. Default: all configured sources.

name: sendOpportunitySms
description: Stage a customer SMS for a Nick's Tire Decision-Inbox opportunity. NEVER sends directly: writes a PENDING ActionReceipt and sends Nour a Telegram Approve/Decline prompt showing the EXACT text — the real send happens only on his Approve tap (nickstire then enforces consent, caps, quiet hours, pause, and dedupe server-side; the send is receipted on the opportunity). CONTRACT: call draftOpportunitySms FIRST, show Nour the draft in chat, apply his edits, and only stage the final text he has seen. Identity comes from the opportunity row — there is no free-form phone targeting. For texting someone NOT in the Decision Inbox, use stageCustomerAlert instead.

body.description: The exact SMS text Nour has seen in chat (edits applied)

customerLabel.description: Short label for the approval prompt, e.g. 'Sam (stale lead)'

name: sendTelegram
description: Send a Telegram message to Nour. Use for proactive alerts, reminders, or important notifications that need to reach his phone.

name: setMit
description: Lock today's Most Important Thing (MIT). Nour picks ONE commitment per day; this tool writes it. Example args: { text: 'Close the Smith estimate before EOD' }

text.description: The single most important thing to get done today

name: setOKRs
description: Set quarterly OKRs (Objectives and Key Results). Use when planning the quarter or when Nour asks about goals/OKRs.

name: setTaskPriority
description: Override the priority of a task to a specific level. Use when Nour explicitly says 'this is critical' / 'low priority' / 'bump priority'. Priority is 0-100 where HIGHER = more urgent (100=drop-everything, 90=critical, 70=high, 50=normal, 30=someday). Example: {"taskId":142,"priority":90}

reason.description: Why Nour set this priority — logged to autoPriorityExplanation for later review.

titleQuery.description: Fuzzy match against active task titles if taskId unknown. Picks the most recently-touched match.

name: setWeeklyTargets
description: Set this week's 3 targets. Call on Monday or when Nour wants to set goals. Stores them so you can reference mid-week.

name: snoozeTask
description: Snooze a task until a future date. Status flips to WAITING + snoozedUntil set · the task-resurface cron flips it back to READY at the wake-up time. Use when Nour says 'snooze this until tomorrow / friday / next week'.

days.description: Days from now to wake up · 1 = tomorrow · 7 = next week

titleQuery.description: Fuzzy match against active task titles if taskId unknown.

name: stageCustomerAlert
description: Stage an SMS outreach to a customer for approval. Writes a PENDING ActionReceipt and sends a Telegram approval prompt to Nour.

phone.description: Phone number in E.164 format or standard 10-digit digits

name: suggestSkills
description: Find the best Claude skills (from the indexed skill registry) for the operator's current task or question. Returns skill name + description + similarity score for top 3 matches. Use when the operator says 'which skill applies here', 'is there a skill for X', or when Nick wants to recommend a specialist lens before answering.

query.description: Task or question to find skills for.

topK.description: Same as limit (the name the retired searchSkills used). limit wins when both are set.

name: summarize
description: Quickly summarize text, emails, documents, or chat threads

name: syncCalendar
description: Manually trigger a Google Calendar ingest — pulls the past 7 days + next 14 days of events into BrainMemory (long-term recall) right now instead of waiting for the scheduled cron. Use when Nour says 'sync my calendar', 'refresh my calendar', or 'pull my latest events'. Returns ingest stats; if OAuth is expired it returns an actionable re-grant hint.

name: syncDriveMemory
description: Manually trigger a Google Drive ingest run — pulls the latest Drive documents, extracts their content, generates embeddings, and stores them as cold memories searchable via searchColdMemory. Use when Nour says 'sync my drive', 'refresh my knowledge base', 'ingest my latest docs', or similar. Returns stats on what was ingested.

force.description: If true, bypass any recency check and re-pull all candidate files. Use sparingly — embeds cost API calls.

name: syncGmail
description: Manually trigger a Gmail ingest — pulls recent messages into statenour-os (classification + BrainMemory) right now instead of waiting for the scheduled cron. Use when Nour says 'sync my gmail', 'refresh my inbox', or 'pull my latest emails'. Returns ingest stats; if OAuth is expired it returns an actionable re-grant hint.

name: syncKnowledge
description: Run the knowledge sync pipeline on demand. Three idempotent stages: (1) promote substantial new chat messages to BrainDumps (AI classification of raw BrainDumps is currently disabled — no provider), (2) rebalance priorities on backfill/journal-sourced tasks, (3) index substantial assistant chat messages as nick_advice memories. Use when Nour says 'sync my knowledge', 'process new thoughts', 'ingest recent chats', or 'catch up the brain'.

name: toolHealth
description: Check the health of Nick's tools and their dependencies. Shows which tools are operational, degraded, or down. Use when Nour asks about system health, tool status, or 'is everything working?'

name: triggerBrief
description: Generate Nour's daily executive brief right now from the latest ingested intelligence, store it, and return the text. Does not re-fetch external sources — use when he asks for 'my brief' / 'the brief' on demand.

name: updateTask
description: Update task fields · partial mutate (only provided fields change). Covers reframe (title / finishCondition), move (missionId), link/unlink goal (goalId), change kind (loopKind), reschedule (dueDate). Use when Nour says 'reframe this as X', 'move to project Y', 'link to goal Z', 'change to a daily'.

goalId.description: Set to null to UNLINK from goal · pass an id to link

loopKind.description: ONCE = one-shot · DAILY = repeats every day · PROMISE = commitment to someone (also send promiseTo).

name: weeklyReview
description: Weekly performance review — 7-day revenue trend, task completion rate, habit streaks, drift patterns, wins and misses

name: writeCreative
description: Write creative content: social posts, ad copy, email subject lines, slogans
